title: A special very ample line has a Clifford support subcurve
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $D$ a nonempty connected projective reduced curve of pure dimension one. Assume all its singular points have completed local ring $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $L$ be a very ample invertible module: the pullback of the hyperplane line by some closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $H^1(D,L)\ne0$, there is a nonempty connected reduced union $Y$ of irreducible components, possibly $Y=D$, such that, with $e=\deg_YL$ measured on normalized components,
$$e\ge2,\qquad h^0(Y,L|_Y)\le\tfrac e2+1.$$
Here cohomology is Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and degree and normalization are [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] [def-sc-normalization]. No GIT hypothesis, fixed Hilbert polynomial or condition on rational tails is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch] to $D$: since $H^1(D,L)\ne0$, there is a nonzero map $\phi:L\to\omega_D$. Among all such maps choose one for which the number of components with nonzero generic map is least. By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $D$ is proper and hence of finite type. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0,k$); [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $D$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finitely many components. Let $Y$ be their reduced union. It is nonempty: in a trivialization a section of an invertible module on a reduced affine scheme vanishing at all minimal primes is zero, since their intersection is the nilradical $0$. The same argument shows $I_Y\phi=0$: its product is zero at every component generic point, either because the ideal is zero there or because $\phi$ is zero there. By [lem-sfb-nodal-subcurve-dualizing-annihilator], $\phi$ therefore comes from a nonzero map $L|_Y\to\omega_Y$.

source.place: Tags 0BS2, 0BS4, 0BS6 and 0E33, combined by the agent minimal-support argument for Morrison Section 3.2 step (7), printed p.14.

proof.text: The connected components of $Y$ are open and closed: grouping its finitely many irreducible components by chains of intersections expresses each group and its complement as finite unions of closed components. $Y$ is connected. Otherwise take a connected component $Y_0$ on which this map is nonzero, retain its restriction and set it to zero on the other connected components of $Y$. These components are open and closed in $Y$, so this defines a map on $Y$. The injection in [lem-sfb-nodal-subcurve-dualizing-annihilator] extends it to a nonzero map on $D$ supported on fewer components, a contradiction. Set $M=L|_Y$, $N=\omega_Y\otimes M^{-1}$ and $W=H^0(Y,N)$. For every nonzero $w\in W$, the corresponding map $M\to\omega_Y$ extends by the same injection to $D$. Minimality forces it to be nonzero at every component generic point of $Y$.

source.place: Tags 0BS2, 0BS4, 0BS6 and 0E33, combined by the agent minimal-support argument for Morrison Section 3.2 step (7), printed p.14.

proof.text: Put $V=H^0(Y,M)$ and $g=h^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. By [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch], all section spaces are finite-dimensional, $\dim W=h^1(Y,M)>0$, $h^0(Y,\omega_Y)=g$, and $\dim V-\dim W=e+1-g$, with exactly the normalized-component degree $e$ in the statement. For $v\ne0$ some generic value of $v$ is nonzero, by reducedness and a local line trivialization. Every $w\ne0$ is nonzero on that component by step 2, so the section product $vw\in H^0(Y,\omega_Y)$ is nonzero. Thus [lem-sfb-hopf-bilinear-image-dimension] applied to multiplication gives $\dim V+\dim W-1\leq g$. Eliminating $\dim W$ gives $2\dim V\leq e+2$.

source.place: Tags 0BS2, 0BS4, 0BS6 and 0E33, combined by the agent minimal-support argument for Morrison Section 3.2 step (7), printed p.14.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], the restriction $M$ is the hyperplane line for the closed immersion of $Y$ obtained by restricting the given immersion of $D$. Hence $\dim V\geq2$: if $V=0$ the coordinate sections cannot generate $M$; if $V$ is one-dimensional, they are all scalar multiples of one generator, which must be nowhere zero, and the immersion is the constant map to the point with those scalar coordinates. Such a map cannot be a closed immersion of a pure one-dimensional nonempty scheme. The inequality of step 3 therefore gives $e\geq2$ and $h^0(Y,M)\leq e/2+1$, as required.
